title: Path to a POSIX kernel with a userspace and a desktop you can build on
outcome: Breenix runs real programs unmodified on ARM64 and x86-64: every POSIX system interface backed and behaving to the standard, a C library and Rust std on top, POSIX utilities, an SDK for building our own applications, and a GPU-rendered graphical desktop (GPU rendering, BreenGL, the window manager and its applications) tested to the same bar.

efforts.title: Kernel bring-up
efforts.outcome: The main-path targets boot to their first userspace process through the boot path's first six milestones. x86-64 bring-up is proved separately on the x86-metal path.
efforts.targetsNote: As of 2026-10-18, x86-64 is measured on bare metal (the x86-metal path), rather than x86 QEMU. x86 hardware-profile milestones remain defined but are measured nowhere on the main path.

efforts.title: GPU rendering
efforts.outcome: Breenix renders on the GPU on every target: a clean-room, GL-style Breenix API whose command streams the kernel validates and bounds per process and translates for VirGL (ARM64 QEMU and Parallels) or SVGA3D DX (VMware), executed by a hardware GPU on each host, presented at 1280×800 and at 2560×1600 with HiDPI scaling, and read back from the device pixel-exact under a declared deterministic rendering profile.
efforts.targetsNote: As of 2026-10-18, x86-64 is measured on bare metal (the x86-metal path), rather than x86 QEMU. x86 hardware-profile milestones remain defined but are measured nowhere on the main path.

efforts.title: Screen console & virtual terminals
efforts.outcome: Every target boots behind an original Breenix logo with live boot progress on its firmware or boot framebuffer, then hands the screen to a text console sized for the display: six virtual terminals with their own screens and scrollback, the kernel log on the first and a login prompt on each in console mode, switched with Alt+F1..F6, Alt+Left/Right, VT_ACTIVATE and chvt, the foreground terminal owning the keyboard, and every screen checked by reading its displayed pixels back against independently expected ones.

efforts.title: Unattended server
efforts.outcome: A persistent Breenix install runs unattended as a LAN server: SSH on port 22 by keys only, supervised services with their own logs, time kept in sync, a clean reboot, a watchdog that brings a hung machine back, and remote upgrades that roll back by themselves when the new install does not answer.

milestones.title: SSH by keys only, with per-install host keys
Per-service logs with rotation and boot IDs
Time synchronized over SNTP, RTC kept in UTC
A hung machine comes back by itself
The persistent install is the resting state

efforts.targetsNote: x86-64 leads on bare metal (the R240): lanes prove there first, then the catch-up brings ARM64 QEMU, Parallels and VMware to the same bar (operator decision D6, 2026-10-20).

efforts.title: Users and permissions
efforts.outcome: Breenix is a multi-user Unix: full credentials and access checks on every path, accounts in /etc/passwd, group and shadow with their own tools, su and a sudo-style admin path, the standard filesystem layout with owners and modes, and the operator logging in to a personal account on the console and over SSH, never as root.

efforts.title: Copy-on-write filesystem
efforts.outcome: Breenix's own copy-on-write B-tree filesystem holds the root and home: atomic commits, checksums on metadata and data with scrub, and snapshots, recovered from power cuts without losing an acknowledged write, with the persistent install migrated onto it from ext2.
